title: Development through a functioning, expanding self
count_correction: The earlier page named 25 abilities under THE 24 and displayed five tiers. All names are preserved here in four stages; none is deleted.
status_policy: This registry defines capabilities and measurements, not passes. A pass requires a linked valid physical result, acquisition, retention and transfer scope.
dependency_policy: mechanisms_required are physical/information prerequisites. helpful_skills are nonblocking learning routes; no fixed infant sequence is imposed.
minimum_environment_scope: Engineering sufficiency hypotheses for motor-learning tests, not infant-care instructions or claims from deprivation experiments. Natural_driver entries are design interpretations, not measured infant motives.

abilities.name: Self / world distinction

human_comparison.text: Birth and early infancy; operational contingency sensitivity is not adult self-recognition.

abilities.natural_driver: Own motion supplies correlated touch and proprioception; the outside world supplies partly independent changes.

minimum_environment.description: A movable body, gravity, a firm noninjurious support, room for limbs and sustained sensorimotor experience. Basic caregiving that sustains a real infant is assumed; active adult instruction is not part of the motor test.

abilities.implementation_gap: A predictable wall is not part of the motor body. Correlation alone cannot distinguish common causes.

tests.question: Select which changes were self-caused when external motion is replayed with matched timing; reverse the action-effect link.

abilities.name: Look at a target and remain on it

human_comparison.text: Oculomotor control develops in early infancy; pursuit and voluntary target choice are separate measurements.

abilities.implementation_gap: Center-of-mass displacement caused by collapse or external forces is not controlled weight shift.

abilities.name: Act before an expected consequence

human_comparison.text: Six-month-olds showed predictive reaching to moving objects in a tested interception task.

abilities.natural_driver: A learned cue can forecast accessible contact, loss of function or another useful bodily consequence before it happens.

abilities.implementation_gap: Pre-event activity alone can be a timer or motion reflex. A violated prediction must change future behavior.

human_comparison.text: Early infant contingency learning motivates testing effect-specific action; batting has no universal mastery date.

abilities.implementation_gap: A higher contact count from indiscriminate movement is not a deliberate strike.

human_comparison.text: Auditory-directed reaches were tested at five and seven months; sound localization and reaching are distinct.

minimum_environments.body_floor: A movable body, gravity, a firm noninjurious support, room for limbs and sustained sensorimotor experience. Basic caregiving that sustains a real infant is assumed; active adult instruction is not part of the motor test.
minimum_environments.one_visible_object: The body and support plus one visible feature or object whose bearing or accessibility can vary. Continuous entertainment, speech and injury are unnecessary for this test.
minimum_environments.one_reachable_object: One physically reachable movable object with observable contact consequences; alternate body sites can supply self-contact experience without an object.
minimum_environments.one_located_sound: One spatially located sound source whose position can vary independently of visible events. Speech is optional for orienting.
minimum_environments.prone_floor: Safe prone support and free arms/head, with ordinary visual and tactile variation. A completed roll is not required to supply a prone starting state.
minimum_environments.graspable_object: One unattached object with size, mass and friction within the hand’s measured grasp envelope.
minimum_environments.object_and_support: A graspable object and a support on which placing it changes load or frees the hand.
minimum_environments.two_hand_object: An object whose size or loading makes coordinated two-hand interaction physically relevant.
minimum_environments.supported_to_free_sitting: A floor and physically attainable seated posture; external placement or temporary support supplies experience but never counts as independent sitting.
minimum_environments.open_floor: Enough floor area and friction for body-length travel with ordinary reachable surfaces or objects. A caregiver can offer destinations but need not continually intervene.
minimum_environments.tool_and_out_of_reach_object: A graspable effective tool, an initially inaccessible consequential object, and real object-object contact; compare ineffective and substitute tools.
minimum_environments.stable_graspable_support: A support reachable from the floor, capable of accepting grip force and body load without hidden attachment.
minimum_environments.flat_floor: A physically attainable upright stance on a supportive floor; a teacher may place the body for practice, but no aid remains during independent balance scoring.
minimum_environments.support_and_open_floor: A rail for cruising and adjacent free floor for distinct independent-step tests; space for balance corrections.

rochat1999.title: Rochat & Striano (1999), Emerging self-exploration by 2-month-old infants
rochat1999.finding: Two-month-olds changed sucking under analog versus random contingent auditory feedback; newborns did not show the same modulation. This is evidence from one agency task, not a complete self concept.

clifton1991.title: Clifton, Rochat, Litovsky & Perris (1991), Object representation guides infants’ reaching in the dark
clifton1991.finding: Six-month-olds’ reaches to sounding objects in darkness were studied after visual experience. Seeing the hand during a reach is not a universal prerequisite for directed action.

clifton1989.title: Development of infant reaching in the dark to luminous objects and invisible sounds (1989)
clifton1989.finding: Auditory-directed reaching was less frequent and poorer than visual-directed reaching in the tested five- and seven-month-old groups; sensory routes can differ.

thelen1996.title: Thelen, Corbetta & Spencer (1996), Development of reaching during the first year
thelen1996.finding: Four infants were followed from reaching onset through the first year. Limb speed and dynamics related to trajectory quality.

thelen1984.title: Thelen, Fisher & Ridley-Johnson (1984), Physical growth and newborn stepping
thelen1984.finding: Adding leg mass reduced stepping; buoyant support increased it. This motivates measuring force, mass and support before attributing immobility to motivation; it is not a rolling experiment.

vonhofsten1998.title: von Hofsten and colleagues (1998), Predictive action in infancy
vonhofsten1998.finding: Six-month-olds tracked and reached for objects on changing trajectories; their actions reflected motion extrapolation. This supports a predictive control test, not a prescribed gaze reward.

corbetta1996.title: Corbetta & Thelen (1996), Developmental origins of bimanual coordination
corbetta1996.finding: Four infants followed through the first year showed changing uni- and bimanual coordination patterns. Development is not a fixed one-hand-then-two-hands program.

who2006.title: WHO Motor Development Study (2006), Windows of achievement
who2006.finding: The study followed 816 children across five countries. Windows overlap; some children did not crawl on hands and knees. The ages in the map are population windows, not required order or simulator deadlines.

fagard2014.title: Fagard, Rat-Fischer & O’Regan (2014), Emergence of rake-like tool use
fagard2014.finding: Successful spatially separated retrieval appeared later than easy contact cases in this longitudinal task. Tool possession or accidental retrieval alone can overstate causal understanding.

adolph2012.title: Adolph and colleagues (2012), How do you learn to walk?
adolph2012.finding: Natural free play supplied variable, distributed practice. Observed twelve- to nineteen-month-olds averaged 2,368 steps per hour; wall-clock training hours are not comparable to this physical experience.

cole2019.title: Where infants go: Real-time dynamics of locomotor exploration (2019)
cole2019.finding: The original study examined natural locomotor exploration, including destinations in the surroundings. Access and exploration are candidate drivers; constant external instruction is not the measured explanation.

adolph1997.title: Adolph (1997), Learning in the development of infant locomotion
adolph1997.finding: Locomotor decisions depend on the infant’s current body, posture and terrain. A capability should be reassessed in a new posture rather than transferred by label.

rachwani2015.title: Rachwani and colleagues (2015), Trunk control and reaching
rachwani2015.finding: Changing the level of external trunk support changed postural instability and reaching. Supported practice can supply experience without counting as unsupported competence.

rolling2004.title: Rolling over in infants: age, ethnicity, and cultural differences (2004)
rolling2004.finding: The observed order of supine-to-prone and prone-to-supine rolling differed from common Western descriptions. Do not impose one universal rolling sequence.

kidd2012.title: Kidd, Piantadosi & Aslin (2012), The Goldilocks effect
kidd2012.finding: Infant looking behavior favored intermediate event complexity in these experiments. This does not establish a universal prediction-error interval or a pleasure equation.

kuhl2003.title: Kuhl, Tsao & Liu (2003), Social interaction and phonetic learning
kuhl2003.finding: In the tested foreign-speech exposure, live interaction supported a phonetic contrast that recordings did not. This motivates a caregiver replay comparison for speech, not a claim that caregivers must direct crawling.

keramati2014.title: Keramati & Gutkin (2014), Homeostatic reinforcement learning
keramati2014.finding: The formal model connects internal physiological state with anticipatory regulation under its assumptions. It does not show that homeostasis alone generates all developmental skills.

patent.title: US11537850B2, Systems and methods for simulating sense data and creating perceptions
patent.finding: The disclosure describes sensory/processing enhancement, impairment and recovery, including changes to resolution. This supplies an embodiment principle, not a validated infant pain law or proof of consciousness.
